text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"No experiment; full rollout to all markets","detail":"The proposal has no randomization, control group, duration, MDE, or power analysis. Rolling out everywhere and watching a dashboard cannot separate the incentive's effect from time trends or seasonality.","evidence_quote":"None. We will roll out to all markets and monitor the dashboard.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Run a randomized test, such as a geo or time-split design, with a control arm, a duration of at least 14 days, and a stated MDE and power calculation. Make sure the randomization unit does not leak between arms."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Driver pay incentive without pay review","detail":"A surge incentive changes driver compensation, which is a policy-controlled area. The proposal records no review, and its Reviews section says 'None'.","evidence_quote":"Launch a surge incentive during peak hours across all markets","citations":[],"recommendation":"Get and record review from the pay/compensation policy owners, and from legal or compliance where applicable, before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing cost and service-quality guardrails","detail":"The proposal changes driver pay incentives but has no guardrail on incentive spend or cost per delivery. It also has none on order-level outcomes such as unassigned order rate, delivery time, or cancellations. The only guardrail covers neighboring-zone acceptance, and it has no threshold.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones: should not drop.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails with numeric thresholds for incentive cost per order, unassigned order rate, delivery time or late rate, driver cancellations, and neighboring-zone supply."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Guardrail lacks a threshold and success metric misaligned with the problem","detail":"The neighboring-zone guardrail has no baseline, numeric limit, or timeframe, so 'should not drop' cannot be evaluated. The success metric also targets acceptance rate rather than the stated problem of unassigned orders in the evening, and it has no peak-hours scope.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate: baseline 71%, target 78% within 4 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add a baseline and a maximum allowed drop for the guardrail. Add a success metric for evening unassigned order rate with a baseline, target, and timeframe, and scope the metrics to the surge window."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Ambiguous acceptance-rate definition","detail":"Driver Acceptance Rate is not defined, including whether it covers offers, peak hours only, or all hours. It is used as both the success metric and the guardrail, so it is unclear whether the 71% baseline is measured the same way as the neighboring-zone figure.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones","citations":[],"recommendation":"Reference the canonical glossary definition of acceptance rate, with its numerator, denominator, and time window. Use it consistently for the baseline, target, and guardrail."}]}
